status.title: Organization status

explain.active: Public pages, listings and ticket sales are on.
explain.limited: Public pages, listings and ticket sales are on, with limits.
explain.suspended: Public pages, listings, the widget and ticket sales are offline and the console is read-only for its members. Tickets already sold stay valid and still scan.
explain.terminated: Closed. Public pages are offline, nothing can be changed, and only its owners can still open the console to export their data. No data was deleted.

effect.suspend: Takes its public pages, marketplace listings, tenant site, widget and checkout offline at once and makes its console read-only. Existing orders stay valid and tickets still scan. The owners are told (without your reason).
effect.reactivate: Brings its public pages, listings and checkout back and makes its console writable again. The owners are told.
effect.terminate: Closes it for good: public pages go offline, ticket scanning stops and members lose the console, except owners, who can still export their data. Only the reviewed restore (runbook, with the platform owner's approval) can undo it. Nothing is deleted.

confirm.suspend: I understand its public pages go offline and its console becomes read-only.
confirm.reactivate: I understand its public pages and checkout come back.

status.adminsOnly: Only admins can change an organization's status.
status.final: Terminated organizations can't be reactivated with these forms. A mistaken termination is restored with the reviewed restore below.

restore.title: Restore a terminated organization
restore.description: Only for a termination that was a mistake, after the platform owner approved restoring it in writing (runbook: “Restore a terminated organization”). Put the approval's reference in the reason.

restore.code: Code from your authenticator app (confirm it's you)
restore.adminsOnly: Only admins can restore an organization.

find.title: Find a person
find.hint: Searches accounts, staff, team invitations, orders, signup codes and security events. The address is sent in the request body, never in a link.

export.title: Export (access request)
export.hint: The same JSON file the person can download from their account page: profile, sessions, security events, organizations and roles, orders and tickets, notification choices, consents and invitations. No passwords, codes or other secrets.

erase.title: Erase (deletion request)
erase.what: Their account is anonymised: signed out everywhere, password and two-step verification removed, name cleared and the email replaced by a hash.
erase.kept: They leave every organization. Organizers keep orders and tickets (legal hold), unlinked from the account.
erase.suppression: The address goes on the platform-wide erased list: no organizer can mail it or import it to a list again unless the person comes back.
erase.final: This can't be undone. A confirmation email goes to the address first.

errors.rate_limited: Too many tries. Wait a few minutes and try again.
errors.two_factor_step_up: That code or password wasn't right. Try again.

platformContent.title: Site content
platformContent.description: What yayatoh.com shows: blog posts, testimonials and the home hero. Changes go live straight away and are recorded in the access log.

done.published: Published. It is live on the site.
done.unpublished: Unpublished. It is a draft again.

error.invalid: Check the fields: a required value is missing or too long.
error.slug: That address is already used by another post.
error.type: That file is not an accepted image or video.
error.too_large: That file is too large (images 5 MB, videos 25 MB).
error.not_image: Choose an image (JPEG, PNG or WebP).

blog.emptyDescription: Write the first post: it appears on /blogs and in the home "Latest from the blog" section once published.
blog.draftHint: Drafts are not shown on the site.

fields.title: Title
fields.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Left empty, it is made from the title.
fields.excerpt: Excerpt (shown on cards and in search results)
fields.bodyHint: Supports **bold**, *italic*, ## headings, - lists and [links](https://…). Raw HTML is shown as text.
fields.coverHint: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB.

testimonials.name: Name
testimonials.emptyDescription: Add one above. Published testimonials appear on the home page.

hero.explain: Empty fields keep the built-in text. With an image or a video, the home hero shows it behind the headline.
hero.headline: Headline
hero.subtitle: Subtitle
hero.imageHint: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB. Also the poster while a video loads.
hero.videoHint: MP4 or WebM, up to 25 MB. Plays muted and looped.
hero.videoUrlHint: Used when no video file is uploaded.
hero.ctaHint: A path on this site (/events) or an https:// link. Text and link go together.

applications.title: Organizer applications
applications.description: People and organizations who applied on the For organizers page or asked for a demo. Approving creates a one-time signup code for the applicant's email and mails the invitation.

approved.title: Approved
approved.body: Approved on the {plan} plan by {who}. The invitation was emailed to the applicant.

approve.title: Approve
approve.help: Creates a one-time signup code that only {email} can use, on the plan you pick, and emails the invitation. After signing up the organization lands on that plan and its setup checklist.
approve.note: Optional note in the invitation email

email.help: This email goes to the applicant exactly as written. Edit it first.
email.subject: Subject

notes.title: Internal notes
notes.label: Add a note (never sent to the applicant)

done.approved_no_email: Approved, but the email could not be sent. Use Resend invitation.
done.resent: A new invitation was emailed; the old code no longer works.
done.needs_info: Email sent and marked Needs info.

error.status: That status change is not allowed.
error.approve: Could not approve (check the plan and the status).
error.resend: Could not resend (the invitation may already be used).
error.email: The email was not sent, so nothing changed.
